title: Login form ships the production super-admin password as a prefilled default
detail: useForm is created with defaultValues: { email: 'admin@barkath.app', password: 'Barkath@123' } (commented 'Dev convenience: prefilled with the seeded super-admin for the emulator'). These are not emulator-only values: /home/h/barkath/scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:22-23 bootstraps the REAL project (barkath-25607) with exactly EMAIL = process.env.ADMIN_EMAIL || 'admin@barkath.app' and PASSWORD = process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD || 'Barkath@123', granting that account role 'super_admin' + fullPerms(). Nothing guards the defaults behind env.useEmulators, so the literals are compiled into the shipped bundle.
failure_scenario: Anyone who opens the deployed admin URL finds email and password already filled and clicks 'Sign in' -> if the project was bootstrapped without ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD overrides they are signed in as a full super admin. Even with an overridden password, the working super-admin username is published in the JS bundle.
fix: Remove defaultValues, or gate them: defaultValues: env.useEmulators ? {seeded creds} : { email: '', password: '' }. Also make scripts/bootstrap-real.ts hard-fail when ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD are unset instead of falling back to the shared literals.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real and unguarded. admin/src/features/auth/components/LoginForm.tsx:30-34 sets useForm defaultValues to {email:'admin@barkath.app', password:'Barkath@123'} with no condition — the codebase has a working guard (env.useEmulators in admin/src/config/env.ts:11, used at admin/src/lib/firebase.ts:19,26) that this call site simply does not use. The literals are not emulator-only: scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:22-23 uses exactly ADMIN_EMAIL||'admin@barkath.app' and ADMIN_PASSWORD||'Barkath@123' when creating the real barkath-25607 super_admin with fullPerms(). Both admin/.env.production and admin/.env.development set VITE_USE_EMULATORS=false and point at project barkath-25607, so even local dev submits these prefilled creds against production. The password is verifiably compiled into the build output: grep finds 'Barkath@123' in admin/dist/assets/index-DQ93d6D0.js:3829. No server-side re-check mitigates it (the creds are genuinely valid, so rules/claims grant super_admin). Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list and not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list (which covers mocked MSG91 OTP for customer login, manual affiliate payouts, Razorpay test mode, App Check — not admin login defaults). Only partial mitigation: firebase.json has no hosting block yet, so the panel may not be publicly deployed today, but a built bundle containing the secret already exists and the fix is one line (remove the defaults or gate on env.useEmulators).

title: No route-level permission guard - sidebar hiding is the only gate, and admin Firestore reads are open to every sub-admin
detail: RequireAuth (admin/src/features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx:6-23) only checks admin != null; it never inspects modulePermissions, and no route carries a module guard. The only client gate is Sidebar.tsx:11-12 (canView) which merely hides nav links. Grepping admin/src shows modulePermissions is referenced in exactly three places (Sidebar.tsx:12, dashboard/components/QuickActions.tsx:42, subadmin form) - no list/detail page checks it. Server-side, firebase/firestore.rules gates only WRITES per module (canWrite); reads are isAdmin(): customers (line 138), orders (line 71), payments (line 84), reviews, orderRequests, commissions, auditLogs all allow any admin. On top of that LoginForm.tsx:41-42 always navigates to '/' after sign-in.
failure_scenario: A sub-admin created with only banner.view signs in -> lands on the full Dashboard (revenue KPIs, recent orders with customer names, low stock) even though 'Dashboard' is hidden from their sidebar. Typing /customers in the address bar renders the complete customer list with every name, phone and email; /orders, /payments, /refunds and /reports work the same way. Nothing on the client or in the rules stops the read.
fix: Add a permission guard component wrapping each route (module key per route, redirecting to a real /403 screen), and land the user on their first permitted route after login instead of '/'. Tighten the isAdmin() read rules on customers/orders/payments/reports collections to can(module,'view').

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute. (1) admin/src/app/router.tsx wraps every page in RequireAuth -> AppShell only; no route has a module guard. (2) RequireAuth.tsx checks `ready` and `admin != null` and nothing else. (3) A full grep of admin/src shows modulePermissions is read only in Sidebar.tsx:12 (nav hiding), dashboard/components/QuickActions.tsx:42 (button hiding), subadmin/routes/SubAdminFormPage.tsx + subadmin/api/subadmin.ts (the editor/type), and account/AccountDialogs.tsx:59 (echoes it back) - no list/detail page, hook, or loader consults it; CustomersListPage.tsx calls useCustomersList() unconditionally on mount. (4) firebase/firestore.rules uses can()/canWrite() exclusively on `allow write`; reads for orders (71), payments (84), customers (138) and its walletTransactions/coupons/notifications subcollections, orderRequests, commissions, withdrawalRequests, spinHistory, reviews, stockAdjustments, broadcasts and auditLogs are plain isAdmin(). isAdmin() is `role == 'super_admin' || role == 'sub_admin'` from the custom claim, and functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:38 sets that claim for every sub-admin, so a banner-only sub-admin passes all of them. Only admins/* and complianceLogs require isSuperAdmin(), so /sub-admin is the sole page that would error; /customers, /orders, /payments, /refunds, /reports and the Dashboard all render real data. The `view` permission is collected and stored by the sub-admin form but enforced nowhere but nav rendering. Not on the already-fixed list (those entries - adminModerateReview, rules canWrite tightening - are write-side) nor the known-intentional list. Only inaccuracy in the claim is cosmetic: LoginForm.tsx:41-42 is `location.state?.from ?? '/'`, not an unconditional '/', but a fresh sign-in still lands on the full Dashboard. Real, fixable defect: needs a route-level module guard plus can(module,'view') on the admin read rules.

title: Suspending a sub-admin does not stop CF-gated actions — requireModule never checks the stored status
detail: requireModule() only calls requireAdmin() (which reads `status` off the *custom claim* in the ID token, guards.ts:21) and then reads `modulePermissions` from admins/{uid}; it never checks `snap.get('status')`. suspendSubAdmin (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:88-96) sets the claim, disables the Auth user and calls revokeRefreshTokens — but firebase-functions v2 `onCall` verifies the ID token WITHOUT checkRevoked (callableOpts in functions/src/_lib/admin.ts:25 sets no such option), so an already-issued ID token stays valid for up to an hour. firestore.rules `can()` (firebase/firestore.rules:23-29) *does* check `adminDoc().status == 'active'`, and functions/src/reviews/moderation.ts:29-31 explicitly re-checks the stored status with the comment "Suspended sub-admins are rejected on the stored doc, not only on the (cacheable) custom claim" — requireModule is the one gate that was never given that check.
failure_scenario: A super admin discovers a rogue ops sub-admin and clicks Sub Admin → ⋮ → Suspend. The toast says "Arjun Rao suspended" and his row flips to Suspended. With his browser tab still open (token minted <60 min ago) he can still call adminDecideReturn (refunds.approve), adminAdjustWallet (customers.edit) and adminUpdateOrderStatus (orders.edit) — i.e. he can keep pushing wallet refunds and money-moving return approvals for up to an hour after being suspended, while the admin UI shows him as locked out.
fix: In requireModule(), after fetching admins/{uid}, reject when `!snap.exists || snap.get('status') !== 'active'` (exactly as requireReviewModeration does), and do the same in requireSuperAdmin by reading the stored doc rather than trusting claims.

verdict.reason:
Could not refute — the claim holds on every point I checked.

1. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/_lib/guards.ts:42-57 — requireModule() calls requireAdmin() (line 47), which only inspects `claims.status` off the ID token (guards.ts:21), then fetches `admins/{uid}` (line 49) and reads ONLY `modulePermissions`. It never reads `snap.get('status')` and never checks `snap.exists`. The doc read is already being paid for, so the missing check is a one-line fix.

2. Token staleness is real, not theoretical. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:88-96 sets the custom claim, calls auth.updateUser({disabled:true}) and revokeRefreshTokens — but firebase-functions v5.1.1 verifies callable tokens at /home/h/barkath/node_modules/.pnpm/firebase-functions@5.1.1_firebase-admin@12.7.0/node_modules/firebase-functions/lib/common/providers/https.js:330 with `verifyIdToken(idToken)` and no checkRevoked argument. Without checkRevoked, verifyIdToken ignores both revocation and the disabled flag, so an already-minted ID token (stale `status:'active'` claim) passes for the remainder of its ~1h life. callableOpts (/home/h/barkath/functions/src/_lib/admin.ts:25-33) sets no option that would change this.

3. The stored-status re-check exists on the two other surfaces, which makes requireModule the odd one out: firebase/firestore.rules can() requires `adminDoc().status == 'active'` for sub-admins, and /home/h/barkath/functions/src/reviews/moderation.ts:29-31 does `if (!snap.exists || snap.get('status') !== 'active') throw` with a comment explicitly stating suspended sub-admins must be rejected on the stored doc rather than the cacheable claim. Same code shape, one gate missing.

4. Blast radius is money-moving, matching the scenario: requireModule is the sole gate on adminAdjustWallet (src/wallet/adjust.ts:23, customers.edit), adminDecideReturn / the second refunds callable (src/returns/decisions.ts:19 and :197, refunds.approve), affiliate withdrawal approve/pay (src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:18,84,98,134), order status/shipment (src/orders/status.ts:54, src/orders/shipment.ts:22), spin grant (src/spin/grant.ts:19), inventory (src/catalog/inventory.ts:26), broadcasts and invoices. None of them re-check status themselves.

5. Not covered by the ALREADY-FIXED list (that list mentions the reviews-only adminModerateReview callable, which is precisely the one that DID get the check) and not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list (App Check being unenforced is unrelated — this is authorization of an authenticated admin, and enforceAppCheck:false is not what lets the stale token through).

Only nuance worth noting: the window is bounded by the token's remaining lifetime (≤1 hour), not indefinite, and the admin client will fail to refresh afterwards. That limits duration, not severity — wallet refunds and return approvals inside that window are irreversible money movement while the UI reports the account as locked out.

title: updateSubAdmin changes role/permissions but never revokes refresh tokens — demoted super admin keeps super_admin for up to an hour
detail: updateSubAdmin calls `auth.setCustomUserClaims(uid, {role, status})` and updates the doc, but unlike suspendSubAdmin (line 92) it never calls `auth.revokeRefreshTokens(uid)`. Custom claims only land in a new ID token, so the target's existing token still carries `role: 'super_admin'`. firestore.rules short-circuits every gate on that claim (`isSuperAdmin()` at line 13, used first in `can()` at line 24) and every CF guard does the same (guards.ts:35, 48), so the stale claim is full authority.
failure_scenario: Super admin A opens Sub Admin → edits super admin B → changes Role to "Sub admin" and leaves only Dashboard on → Save changes. The list immediately shows B as Sub admin. B, still signed in, is unaffected for up to 60 minutes: `isSuperAdmin()` is still true in rules so he can rewrite settings/GST, products and coupons, and `requireSuperAdmin` still passes so he can call createSubAdmin and mint himself a brand-new super-admin account — permanently defeating the demotion.
fix: Call `await auth.revokeRefreshTokens(uid)` in updateSubAdmin whenever role (or modulePermissions) changes, and stamp tokenRevokedAt, mirroring suspendSubAdmin.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:67 updateSubAdmin only calls setCustomUserClaims + ref.update — no revokeRefreshTokens, no disable, and it never stamps tokenRevokedAt (that field is written solely by suspendSubAdmin at line 95, which does revoke at line 92), so the asymmetry is real. The stale claim is full authority on both surfaces: guards.ts reads req.auth.token only (requireAdmin:17-24), requireSuperAdmin:35 gates on claims.role, and requireModule:48 short-circuits for super_admin without reading the admins doc — so a demoted B can still call createSubAdmin and mint a fresh super admin. firestore.rules does the same: role() is request.auth.token.role, isSuperAdmin() is claim-only, and can() short-circuits on isSuperAdmin() before the live adminDoc() branch, so the immediately-updated modulePermissions never gets consulted for a stale super_admin token. No compensating mechanism anywhere: grep across functions/, admin/, web/, app/, packages/shared, scripts/ shows revokeRefreshTokens only in subAdmins.ts:92 and customers/moderation.ts:29, and tokenRevokedAt is never read by rules or any client. The admin client force-refreshes the token only at sign-in (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:50) with no live admins-doc listener, and RequireModule.tsx:24 bypasses UI gating for role==='super_admin'. The path is reachable: SubAdminFormPage.tsx:102 submits an editable role and the callable's RoleSchema accepts both values. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Caveat (severity, not validity): revokeRefreshTokens alone does not invalidate an already-issued ID token for Firestore rules or callables — a complete fix needs revoke plus tokenRevokedAt/auth_time enforcement in rules or a server-side role re-read in guards — but doing nothing at all on demotion is a genuine, fixable privilege-persistence window of up to ~1 hour.

title: NotificationBell is never mounted, and nothing ever writes adminAlerts
detail: The top bar's right cluster renders only <ProfileMenu /> with the comment 'matching the prototype (no bell)'. Grepping the whole repo for 'NotificationBell' returns exactly one hit - its own declaration at admin/src/components/layout/NotificationBell.tsx:66 - so the component, its adminAlerts listener, the unread dot, 'Mark all as read' and the deep-link handler are all unreachable dead code. Even if it were mounted it would always be empty: firebase/firestore.rules:213-218 sets 'allow create: if false' on adminAlerts/{uid}/alerts and no Cloud Function writes them (only scripts/seed.ts:862 does, for the emulator). The seeded alerts also deep-link to '/returns' (seed.ts:858) which is not a route - the module is mounted at '/refunds' (router.tsx:78).
failure_scenario: An admin looks for the notification bell described in the spec and there is none in the top bar; low-stock, new-order, withdrawal and return alerts are never surfaced anywhere in the panel. If the bell is re-added, in production it shows 'You're all caught up.' forever because no CF ever creates an alert, and the seeded 'New return request' row navigates to /returns which the wildcard route silently bounces to the dashboard.
fix: Render <NotificationBell /> in TopBar's right cluster; add CF writes to adminAlerts (order placed, low stock, withdrawal request, return request) via the admin SDK; fix the seeded deepLink '/returns' -> '/refunds'.

verdict.reason: Claim holds on every point. (1) NotificationBell is genuinely unmounted: repo-wide grep yields only its own declaration at admin/src/components/layout/NotificationBell.tsx:66; AppShell.tsx and app/router.tsx never import it and there is no barrel file in components/layout/. (2) The "matching the prototype (no bell)" comment at TopBar.tsx:71 is factually wrong — designs/Barakath Admin Prototype.dc.html renders, in the top bar's right cluster (margin-left:auto, gap:18px), an Icon name="NotificationLine" size="20" with an absolutely positioned unread dot, exactly matching what NotificationBell renders. TopBar's own JSDoc likewise says "breadcrumb + search + bell + profile", contradicting the inline comment. (3) No producer exists: `grep -rli alert functions/src` returns 0 files, so no Cloud Function writes adminAlerts; firestore.rules:213-218 sets `allow create, delete: if false` (its own comment says "CF-authored", i.e. a writer was intended but never built); the only writer in the repo is the emulator seed at scripts/seed.ts:862. So even if mounted the bell would show "You're all caught up." forever in production. (4) Deep-link mismatch confirmed: seed.ts:858 uses '/returns' but the returns module is mounted at '/refunds' (router.tsx:78) and router.tsx:107 wildcard-redirects to '/'. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists; not handled elsewhere — web/ and app/ use customers/{uid}/notifications (customer inbox), and admin's /notifications route is the outbound broadcast composer, neither of which surfaces low-stock/new-order/withdrawal/return admin alerts. Real, fixable defect: mount the bell, emit alerts from the relevant CFs (or delete the component and rules block), and fix the seed deep link to /refunds.

title: lastLoginAt / lastActiveAt are read on two screens but never written at sign-in
detail: signInAdmin() reads admins/{uid}, checks status and refreshes the token, but never stamps lastLoginAt/lastActiveAt; initAuthListener (authStore.ts:28-53) doesn't either. firebase/firestore.rules:199-208 was specifically opened up for exactly this ('Sign-in activity stamps are the ONE thing an admin may write on their own doc ... every row read never'), and that allowance is unused - grep for lastLoginAt across admin/src finds only readers. No CF writes it either: functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:44 sets lastLoginAt: null at creation and never updates it, and there is no blocking-auth trigger.
failure_scenario: A super admin creates a sub-admin, the sub-admin signs in daily for a week, then the super admin opens Sub Admin -> the 'Last active' column (SubAdminListPage.tsx:140, which falls back lastActiveAt -> lastLoginAt) still shows the value stamped at creation time and never moves. Profile menu -> Profile shows 'Last login: -' permanently (AccountDialogs.tsx:95).
fix: In signInAdmin, after the admins doc check, updateDoc(doc(db,'admins',uid), { lastLoginAt: serverTimestamp(), lastActiveAt: serverTimestamp() }) - the rules already permit exactly these two fields with request.time.

verdict.reason: Claim verified. signInAdmin() (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:39-51) only imports `doc, getDoc` and performs no write; initAuthListener (authStore.ts) likewise only reads via loadAdminDoc. Repo-wide grep for lastLoginAt/lastActiveAt finds writers ONLY on the customers collection (web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:76-77, app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:272-273) — a different doc type (packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:143-144), not admins. On the admin side, functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:44 sets lastLoginAt: null / lastActiveAt: now once at creation and the update/suspend/delete CFs never touch them; there is no blocking-auth trigger (no beforeSignIn/beforeUserSignedIn/blockingFunctions in functions/src or firebase.json). firebase/firestore.rules:199-208 explicitly permits self-update of exactly ['lastLoginAt','lastActiveAt'] with request.time, and that allowance has no caller. Readers are real: SubAdminListPage.tsx:140 falls back lastActiveAt -> lastLoginAt and renders timeAgo/"Never signed in", and AccountDialogs.tsx:95 renders "Last login:" which stays "-" forever because the field is created null (seed.ts:91-92 also seeds null). Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists. Real, fixable defect: the Sub Admin "Last active" column shows creation-time forever and Profile shows no last login; fix is a best-effort updateDoc with serverTimestamp() at the end of signInAdmin, already allowed by the rules.

title: Login page advertises two-factor authentication that does not exist anywhere
detail: The sign-in card renders a shield badge reading 'Protected by two-factor authentication'. There is no MFA anywhere in the codebase: signInAdmin (features/auth/api/auth.ts:18-52) does plain signInWithEmailAndPassword with no multiFactor resolver, no TOTP/SMS challenge screen exists, and there is no enrollment UI. The Admin type carries mfaEnrolled / mfaMethod / mfaEnrolledAt (packages/shared/src/types/admin.ts:28-30) which functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:43 writes as false/null on create and which no surface (admin, web, app, functions, rules) ever reads or updates.
failure_scenario: An admin (or a security reviewer) reads the login screen and believes accounts are protected by a second factor; in reality a leaked or guessed password is the only credential needed. The mfaEnrolled column stays false for every admin forever with no way to enrol.
fix: Either remove the badge text, or implement Firebase Auth multi-factor (TOTP) enrolment in the Profile dialog and a challenge step in signInAdmin, and start reading/writing mfaEnrolled/mfaMethod/mfaEnrolledAt.

verdict.reason: Claim verified; refutation attempts failed. admin/src/features/auth/routes/LoginPage.tsx:65-68 renders the present-tense assertion "Protected by two-factor authentication" under the sign-in form. signInAdmin (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:18-52) is plain signInWithEmailAndPassword plus an admins/{uid} status check — no getMultiFactorResolver, and its error switch does not even handle auth/multi-factor-auth-required, so if Identity Platform MFA were enforced project-side login would dead-end on the generic "Could not sign in" branch. The auth feature has only 5 files: no challenge screen, no enrollment screen. A repo-wide grep for mfa|multifactor|two-factor|2fa|totp|authenticator across admin/, web/, app/, functions/, packages/, firebase/*.rules, scripts/ and e2e/ yields only the type declaration (packages/shared/src/types/admin.ts:28-30) and three write sites hardcoding false/null (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:43, scripts/seed.ts:86-88, scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:54-56) — zero readers anywhere; the web/app OTP hits are the unrelated customer phone-login flow, and firestore.rules/storage.rules contain no mfa or factor token. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list and not on the KNOWN+INTENTIONAL list (which covers customer MSG91 OTP mocking, IFSC, manual affiliate payouts, Razorpay test mode and App Check — not MFA), and neither audit/AUDIT.md nor README.md documents it as a deliberate deferral. I declined to refute as "purely cosmetic" because this is a false factual security assertion, not styling — the sibling badge "Role-based access, fully audited" (line 37) IS backed by real role and audit-log machinery, making this the outlier — and a leaked or guessed password is the only credential guarding a panel with money-touching callables. One inaccuracy in the claim: there is no rendered mfaEnrolled column (admin/src never references the field), so that half of the failure scenario overstates; the substance holds. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the finding is misleading UI copy plus dead schema rather than broken logic; the underlying facts are certain. Fix: delete LoginPage.tsx lines 65-68, or implement enrolment and drop the three dead fields if the schema slot is not being reserved deliberately.

title: The subAdmin module permission is a dead toggle — granting it produces a nav item that always errors
detail: The matrix exposes a "Sub Admin" toggle (MODULE_LABELS.subAdmin, subadmin.ts:55) and Sidebar.tsx:11-12 shows the nav entry whenever modulePermissions.subAdmin.view is true. But nothing honours that permission: firebase/firestore.rules:196-198 allows reading admins/{adminUid} only `if isSuperAdmin() || (role()=='sub_admin' && uid()==adminUid)`, so useAdminsList()'s collection query (subadmin.ts:19-21) is denied for every sub-admin; and all four callables (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:22, 52, 77, 102) use requireSuperAdmin, never requireModule(req,'subAdmin',…). No `requireModule` call anywhere in functions/src references 'subAdmin'.
failure_scenario: A super admin turns on "Sub Admin" for a team-lead sub-admin and tells them to manage the team. The lead signs in, sees the Sub Admin nav item, clicks it and gets the permanent error row "Couldn’t load admins. Please try again." Clicking "+ Create admin" still renders the whole form; after filling name/email/password and every module toggle, Save produces "You don’t have permission to create this admin." The toggle can never do anything.
fix: Either enforce the module server-side (rules: allow list on /admins if can('subAdmin','view'); callables: requireModule(req,'subAdmin', create|edit|delete) instead of requireSuperAdmin) or remove 'subAdmin' from MODULE_KEYS/the matrix and hide the nav item for non-super-admins.

verdict.reason: Every link in the claim checks out. `subAdmin` is a grantable toggle (SubAdminFormPage.tsx:210 maps all MODULE_KEYS with no filtering), and both client gates honour it: Sidebar.tsx:11-12 shows the nav item and RequireModule.tsx lets `/sub-admin` mount when `modulePermissions.subAdmin.view` is true. Nothing downstream honours it: firestore.rules admins block allows read only `if isSuperAdmin() || (role()=='sub_admin' && uid()==adminUid)`, which a collection list query (subadmin.ts:19-21) can never satisfy, so useAdminsList() is denied and SubAdminListPage.tsx:126 renders the permanent error row; and all four callables in functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts (lines 22, 52, 77, 102) begin with requireSuperAdmin, so create/update/suspend/delete throw permission-denied, which cfError renders verbatim as "You don't have permission to create this admin." requireModule exists (guards.ts:42) and is used for 7 other modules but never for 'subAdmin'. Greps across functions/, packages/shared/, web/ and app/ find 'subAdmin' only in enums.ts:272 (MODULE_KEYS) and the two admin UI sites — no other surface reads it, no server-side re-check, no fallback. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists; the path is trivially reachable. Real, fixable dead-control defect: either gate the toggle/nav to super admins or teach the rules + callables to accept subAdmin module permissions.

title: Permission/role changes never reach a live session - the auth store snapshots admins/{uid} once at boot
detail: initAuthListener calls loadAdminDoc(uid) exactly once inside onAuthStateChanged and stores the plain object; there is no onSnapshot on admins/{uid}. Sidebar.tsx:12 and QuickActions.tsx:42 read modulePermissions from that frozen object. updateSubAdmin (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:52-73) changes role/modulePermissions and re-sets custom claims but does NOT call revokeRefreshTokens, so the client is never nudged to re-read.
failure_scenario: A super admin revokes the 'Coupons' module from a sub-admin who is currently signed in. The sub-admin's sidebar keeps showing Coupons for the rest of their session; they open it, edit a coupon and hit Save, and only then get a 'You don't have permission' toast from the rules (can() reads the live doc). Conversely, granting a new module doesn't make the nav item appear until a hard reload, so the admin reports the grant 'didn't work'.
fix: Replace the one-shot loadAdminDoc with an onSnapshot on admins/{uid} that updates the store (and signs the user out when status flips to 'suspended'), so nav and quick actions track permissions live.

verdict.reason: Verified in code and could not refute. admin/src/features/auth/stores/authStore.ts:28-52 does a one-shot getDoc via loadAdminDoc (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:54) inside onAuthStateChanged and stores the plain object; there is no onSnapshot/onIdTokenChanged/poll anywhere in admin/src for admins/{uid}, and initAuthListener is mounted once with [] deps in admin/src/app/providers.tsx:8. Sidebar.tsx:12 and QuickActions.tsx:42 are the only modulePermissions consumers and there is no route-level permission guard (RequireAuth only checks admin != null), so a revoked module stays clickable and a granted module stays invisible for the whole session until a hard reload. functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:66-72 (updateSubAdmin) sets custom claims and updates the doc but never calls revokeRefreshTokens — unlike suspendSubAdmin (line 96), which does revoke + disable, so the security-critical suspension case IS handled but permission/role edits are not. That omission adds a real, non-cosmetic consequence the claim only hints at: demoting super_admin -> sub_admin leaves role:'super_admin' in the ID token for up to ~1h, and isSuperAdmin() short-circuits both can() in firebase/firestore.rules and requireSuperAdmin() in functions/src/_lib/guards.ts, so the demoted admin retains full super-admin write power (including self re-promotion) during that window. Mitigating context, hence medium confidence: server-side enforcement is live for module perms (rules can() and guards.ts:50 read the current admins doc), and module 'view' gating is already cosmetic because admin reads are gated only by isAdmin() — so the sidebar half is a UX/staleness defect rather than an access-control hole. Fix is trivial (swap getDoc for onSnapshot on admins/{uid}, and call revokeRefreshTokens in updateSubAdmin when role changes).

title: createSubAdmin leaves an orphan Auth user and permanently burns the email if the Firestore write fails
detail: auth.createUser() runs first (line 34), then setCustomUserClaims (38) and the admins/{uid} doc write (40-46) with no transaction, no rollback and no try/catch. If any step after createUser fails, the Auth account exists with no admin doc. Worse, the create is wrapped in a bare `catch { throw new HttpsError('already-exists', 'An account with that email already exists.') }` — every createUser failure (quota, network, invalid password policy) is reported to the operator as a duplicate email.
failure_scenario: An operator fills Create sub admin and hits Create admin; the Auth user is created, then the Firestore write fails (transient/rules/quota) and the toast shows a generic failure. They retry with the same email: createUser now throws for real and the UI says "An account with that email already exists." — but no row appears in the Sub Admin list, so the email is unusable forever and an Auth account exists that can authenticate yet is rejected by signInAdmin ("Not authorized to access admin panel") with no admin-panel way to see or delete it.
fix: Wrap the post-createUser steps in try/catch and `auth.deleteUser(user.uid)` on failure; distinguish the real `auth/email-already-exists` code from other createUser errors instead of a blanket catch.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:32-46 creates the Auth user, then sets claims and writes admins/{uid} with no try/catch and no compensating auth.deleteUser, and the bare `catch` at 35-37 discards the real error (no logging) and reports every createUser failure as 'already-exists'. No mitigation exists elsewhere: no getUserByEmail / beforeUserCreated / auth onCreate trigger anywhere in functions/src, so nothing back-fills the admins doc; the Sub Admin list (admin/src/features/subadmin/api/subadmin.ts:19) reads only collection('admins'), so an orphan Auth user is invisible; and deleteSubAdmin (subAdmins.ts:109-110) throws not-found before reaching auth.deleteUser when the admins doc is missing, so the orphan cannot be removed from the panel. signInAdmin (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:38-42) rejects it with 'Not authorized to access admin panel.' exactly as described. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists; sibling handlers in the same file explicitly tolerate partial failure (lines 91, 113) while the create path does not. Confidence is medium only because zod pre-validation makes the non-duplicate createUser failure a transient/quota window rather than a deterministic path — that lowers likelihood, not validity, and the fix (rollback on failure + map only auth/email-already-exists) is small.

title: Permission and role changes never reach an already-open sub-admin session — the auth store snapshot is read once
detail: initAuthListener calls loadAdminDoc(uid) once per onAuthStateChanged event (a one-shot getDoc, features/auth/api/auth.ts:52-55) and stores the plain object; there is no onSnapshot on admins/{uid}. Sidebar.tsx:11 and QuickActions.tsx:42 read that frozen object, so a permission edit made by updateSubAdmin is invisible to the target until they hard-reload the tab, while firestore.rules `can()` re-reads the live doc on every write.
failure_scenario: A super admin removes the Coupons module from a sub-admin who is signed in. The sub-admin's sidebar still shows Coupons; they open a coupon, edit the discount cap and hit Save — the direct Firestore write is rejected by canWrite('coupons') and they get a generic failure toast on a screen they are still being shown, with no indication their access was revoked.
fix: Subscribe to admins/{uid} with onSnapshot in initAuthListener and push updates into the store (also signing the user out when status flips to 'suspended').

verdict.reason: Confirmed. authStore.ts:27-56 loads admins/{uid} via a one-shot getDoc (auth.ts:76-79) inside onAuthStateChanged, which fires only on sign-in/sign-out, and no onSnapshot on admins/{uid} exists anywhere in admin/src (grep for onSnapshot yields only NotificationBell and firestoreCache). The store is only otherwise rewritten by LoginForm.tsx:40 and AccountDialogs.tsx:62 (own-profile save), neither of which covers a super-admin permission edit. No fallback guard rescues it: RequireModule.tsx:21 reads the very same frozen object, so the route guard is stale exactly like Sidebar.tsx:11 and QuickActions.tsx:42. Server-side enforcement is real but is what creates the dead end — firestore.rules can()/canWrite() (lines 29-40) get() the live doc on every write, coupons are a direct client write (coupons.ts:141,153), and CouponFormPage.tsx:181 surfaces the raw "Missing or insufficient permissions" as a generic toast. updateSubAdmin (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:51-74) sets custom claims but never calls revokeRefreshTokens — only suspendSubAdmin (line 92) does, which is why suspension self-corrects and permission edits do not. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and no UI copy warns that changes need a re-login. Rules line 214-216 let a sub_admin read their own doc, so an onSnapshot fix is legal and small. Mitigating note: this is not a privilege-escalation hole — impact is stale nav, lost work, and an opaque error until a hard reload.
